_comment: The sg-succession subject sidecar. FOUR Singapore Acts, encoded as ONE
subject against one shared ontology, because they are four views of one
event -- a death in a family -- and they share their nouns. See NOTES.md
for why that is not four subjects, and for the L4 traps this corpus paid
for.
THE SUBJECT IS FOUR ACTS; THE PRIMARY ENCODING COVERS THREE. The
Guardianship of Infants Act 1934 was added to the subject on 2026-08-26
and is encoded only in 'cleanroom-2026-08'. Read 'encoding' (singular, the
committed corpus) as the Wills / Intestate Succession / Probate trio and
nothing more; a reader who takes the widened display_name as a claim about
the committed modules would be wrong, which is why this paragraph is here
and not in a commit message.
'encoding.modules' is listed IN DEPENDENCY ORDER: the domain module
declares the types the three Act modules import, sg-succession composes
them, and the case suite exercises the composition.
'checks.min_dated_arms' is 0 ON PURPOSE, for both encodings. Neither
carries a rule-version axis: each states the law as at its source bundle's
in-force date and has no 'RULES EFFECTIVE DATE' arms at all. A 0 floor
makes p3-check report the temporal-closure sub-check NOT CHECKED rather
than vacuously green over an empty matched set. Raise it the day a corpus
gains dated arms; never lower a floor to make a run pass.
'checks.min_assertions' is 178 for the committed encoding = the
assertions_total that 'l4 run --json' reports across its module set.
The floor exists because 'no failed assertion' is satisfied vacuously by
an empty results[].
RE-MEASURED 2026-08-20, per module, via etc/go/lib/assert-report.mjs over
`l4 run --json` envelopes: sg-wills 62 + sg-paa 79 + sg-succession-cases 37
= 178, with 0 failed. The other four modules contribute none -- including
sg-isa, whose section 7 distribution rules are exercised entirely from
sg-succession-cases.l4 rather than in place.
This comment previously read '131 = ... (sg-wills 39 + sg-paa 55 + cases
37)', which was both stale against the declared 178 AND wrong in its own
arithmetic for the corpus as it then stood. It was left behind when the
corpus grew; the declared floor was updated and the sentence explaining it
was not, which is the drift that makes a comment worse than no comment.
FLOORS TRAVEL WITH THEIR ENCODING, structurally: encodings.<id>.checks
sits inside the encoding it measures, so the committed floor of 178 can
never be applied to the cleanroom deposit and the cleanroom's 1789 can
never be applied to the committed corpus, which would let it shrink
unnoticed.
'encodings.cleanroom-2026-08.checks.min_assertions' is 1789, MEASURED
2026-08-26 with assert-report.mjs over `l4 run --json` for all six modules:
wills-act 341 + intestate-succession-act 381 +
probate-administration-act 429 + guardianship-of-infants-act 404 +
family-cases 234 = 1789, 0 failed; family-domain contributes none, being
types only. The same 1789 appears in the committed .golden files.
'natlang_sources' and 'comparison' now point at the CLEANROOM registers,
which cover four Acts as retrieved on 26 Aug 2026 and supersede the
three-Act ones under denovo/ (retrieved 18 Aug 2026). Those files are left
on disk as the record of what was deposited then; they are no longer
declared, and the fork register that replaced them says so in its own note
-- the two are not versions of each other, because they describe forks in
two independently written encodings.
'comparison.surface_map' is declared before it exists, which the deposit
contract allows: p8-diff reports SKIPPED naming the missing path rather
than pretending the comparison was made.
